# The DoCoDeGo System

**Dual Operating Composition Demonstration and Governance System**

**Version:** 1.2.5 · **Status:** Canonical · **Licence:** CC BY 4.0

The DoCoDeGo System is the operating model for building products when machines do the
making. It does not do the work. It keeps the work in order: an intent written precisely
enough that a machine can act on it and a person can check it; work made inside a structure
a person declared; proof that ran and that a stranger can check; and a named person's
signature on every unit. Its record — the trail kept beside the work — is the system of
record: append-only, evidence-linked, readable cold.

## The axiom

**Intent is the primary artifact. Implementation is a compiled derivative. Governance is
earned through the loop.**

A stance, not a description of today. This is not a claim that code no longer matters, or
that the world already works this way.

## The plain form and the question

*Mean it. Make it. Prove it. Own it.* One verb per movement: DO, CO, DE, GO.

The question, asked of the work at every step: ***can you stand behind it?*** To stand
behind something means to answer for it: to support it, to be responsible for it, and to be
able to take some quiet pride in it. Answered at the end of every unit by a named person's
signature. The question is asked of the work, never of a person's worth.

## The four values

Intent over Implementation. Direction over Production. Flow over Releases. Governance over
Process. Both sides matter; this is an order of priority.

## The loop on one page

Four movements, sixteen streams, one shape at every scale:

| Movement | Verb | Streams | Question |
|---|---|---|---|
| **DO** Document | mean it | discover · refine · validate · plan | what is the intent? |
| **CO** Compose | make it | build · integrate · enhance · maintain | how is it made? |
| **DE** Demonstrate | prove it | demo · accept · release · deploy | what evidence shows it matches? |
| **GO** Govern | own it | monitor · measure · retrospect · improve | who answers for it? |

Govern runs through everything: plan approval, the grilling's threat question, acceptance,
the signature on every receipt, and the authority to halt at any point. Improve feeds the
next refine, so the loop closes. This is not four phases in a line: every unit runs the
whole loop, quickly, and one person can do all four before lunch.

## The gates

A spec passes a structural check, then the Intent Clarity Score (completeness, testability,
unambiguity, threat coverage; at least 60 of 100 to build, at least 15 of 25 on threat
coverage, no dimension at zero). Grilling: ten to fifteen hard questions from someone other
than the author, every question answered. Proofs: evidence that ran, witnessed, bound to the
exact work, checkable by a stranger. The receipt: the unit's last act — proofs, spec
version, what it taught, and the signature of a named person. The score is a gate, not a
target. See [conformance/gates-and-severity.md](conformance/gates-and-severity.md).

## What the System is not

Not a tool (no product, model or vendor required — there is no official way). Not a
certification (nobody is certified in it, including its authors). Not a process with one
correct form ("only more or less aligned ones"). Not Agile with new names. Not Waterfall
(nothing waits for a phase to end). Not spec-driven development as currently packaged (the
spec is one part; the decision with its reason, the proof that ran, the signature, the
signal after release and the lesson filed are the rest). Not contingent on machines staying
limited. Not finished — this document is versioned, and each version says what changed and
why. Not a ranking — its measures never compare people or teams. Not a reason to slow down.

Wrong answer for: throwaway work, pure exploration, prototypes nobody will sign. Sketch
those freely; graduate the survivors.

## Anti-capture

1. **No certification.** No mark, badge or seal of any kind.
2. **No tool required.** Practised on paper, in plain files, or with any tool.
3. **No ranking of people.** Measures are for learning about the work.
4. **No one to ask.** No permission, licence or trainer needed.
5. **Many loops, not one big one.** Scaling means more units and more trails read together,
   not layers of governance stacked on top. A framework that adds layers above the loop is
   something else.

## The name

DoCoDeGo is an anagram of *Good Code*. The name is the claim. The practice is the proof.

## Reading order

Newcomers: this page, then [movements/the-loop.md](movements/the-loop.md), then
[record/the-trail.md](record/the-trail.md), then the statutes ([laws/](laws/)). Tooling:
[conformance/](conformance/). Maintainers: [meta/how-to-amend.md](meta/how-to-amend.md).
The glossary lives at [meta/terminology.md](meta/terminology.md).

## How to cite

Every law carries a stable anchor (`ST-1`…`ST-16` for the sixteen statutes, `EL-17`… for
engine laws). Cite the anchor: "per ST-15, every specification includes a threat model."
Retired anchors keep their numbers.
